$comment: The Google identity surface of the two Android apps, recorded once so that
a machine can check it. Two facts live here that no test could otherwise
know: which signing fingerprints are LEGITIMATELY registered against our
OAuth clients, and whether Play App Signing has been enrolled yet.
Why it matters: Google matches an Android sign-in request by (package name,
signing certificate SHA-1). Today the only fingerprint registered for either
package is a DEVELOPMENT keystore. Every build the owner tests signs with it
and signs in perfectly. The store build is signed by Google with a different
key and matches no OAuth client.
**And the user is shown nothing.** Under Credential Manager (google_sign_in
v7) a wrong signing SHA comes back as `canceled`, which the plugin cannot
tell from a dismissal — docs/design/app-google-signin-v7.md §9 says so, and
that is the reason it says so. api_auth_service.dart:189 maps it to code
'cancelled' with an EMPTY message, and auth_provider.dart:141 sets _error =
null for that code. No banner, no log, no crash: the button simply does
nothing, forever. The success case and the failure case are the same code
path, and the failure case is silent.
google-services.json is generated from console state and emits one
oauth_client entry with client_type 1 per registered fingerprint, so the
committed file is a faithful (if possibly stale) mirror of what Google will
accept. A stale file makes the gate refuse a release that would have worked,
which is the safe direction to be wrong in: the fix is to re-download.

howToGetIt: Do NOT transcribe this from a Play Console page — that method produced a
wrong value twice on 2026-08-26 (the upload key, then another generated
certificate from the same page). Read it off the artifact Google actually
1. Roll the release out to yourself on the internal track, install it
on a phone THROUGH PLAY, enable USB debugging, plug in.
2. adb pull "$(adb shell pm path <package> | sed 's/package://' | head -1)" app.apk
NOT the source stamp — both say CN=Android/O=Google)
4. Register that SHA-1 as an Android OAuth client in the GCP console
(Firebase fingerprint auto-provisioning did NOT create OAuth clients
when tried; manual creation worked instantly), and mirror it in the
Firebase app's fingerprint list so that registry tells the truth too.
5. Store it here lowercase with the colons stripped, the way
google-services.json stores it, then re-download each config and
commit it, or the gate stays red.
playAppSigning.$comment: sha1 used to live here, singular — one-key assumption, wrong: Play generated one key per app. And the first per-package values recorded were wrong TOO: read off the Play Console App-signing page, they matched nothing Google serves (sign-in failed with UNREGISTERED_ON_API_CONSOLE until the true certificates were read from the DELIVERED artifact). Console-page transcription produced a wrong value twice in one day — first the upload key (shared across apps, since one keystore signs both uploads), then whatever generated-certificate block 4d3d…/a161… came from. The values below came from the installed bytes; see howToGetIt.

$comment: Which OAuth client id the apps present as the `aud` of a Google ID token.
The backend's GoogleIdTokenVerifier accepts only the ids in the
GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS secret and rejects everything else, so an audience that
is not in that list is a sign-in that fails AFTER Google succeeds: the user
sees the Google sheet, picks an account, and lands back on an error.
**Both platforms send `server`, not their own client id.** The app passes
serverClientId to GoogleSignIn.instance.initialize, and that argument sets
the audience on BOTH platforms — not only Android. Verified from source
rather than assumed, because assuming it was how this file first got it
wrong: google_sign_in_ios-6.3.0 FLTGoogleSignInPlugin.m:344 forwards it into
GIDConfiguration, whose header says of serverClientID `This will be returned
as the audience property of the OpenID Connect ID token`, and GIDSignIn.m:901
sets additionalParameters[@"audience"] from it.
So `clients` below is NOT an allowlist requirement. Those four ids are what
each build carries as its OWN identity (azp), and they are recorded so the
checks can tell that the committed configs still match. Requiring them in
GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS would refuse a release that works perfectly.
The load-bearing invariant is conditional, and the check evaluates it that
way: WHILE the app passes serverClientId the audience is `server`; if that
argument is ever dropped, the audience silently becomes the per-flavour id
and every one of those must then be allowlisted instead.
